title: Four Hundred Feet of Light
hook: Nobody out here for fifty miles.
scene: I-90 east of Ellensburg, straight to a horizon that is only dark. Nobody out here for fifty miles, so the high beams go on and the road ahead turns into a tunnel of light with a hard black edge. The book's number is four hundred feet — the glow you have to be able to stop inside. Past that edge you are driving on arithmetic and hope, and somewhere past it is the rest area and a body that has been awake since dawn.
decision: Two hours of dark in front of you. What is the drive?

options.text: High beams and hold seventy — you can see forever now.
options.result: High beams show you more road, not more stopping distance. At seventy the car needs further than the light reaches, and the shadow outruns the beams. Seeing farther is not a reason to go faster.

options.text: Low beams the whole way — high beams are rude.
options.result: There is nobody to be rude to for fifty miles. High beams on an open road with no oncoming traffic are the tool, and dipping them for every rise just shortens the light you have.

options.text: Keep the beams up and skip the rest area — momentum is sleep.
options.result: Momentum is not sleep. Heavy eyes, drifting, missing the last few miles: that is the list, and you are on it. A twenty-minute nap at the rest area is the cheapest thing you will do all night.

options.text: High beams when the road is empty, low beams when it isn't — and stop inside the light.
options.result: High beams out here, dimmed the moment there is traffic to blind, and a speed that keeps the shadow inside the glow — four hundred feet of light and a car that can stop in it. When the eyes go heavy, the rest area is the answer, not the radio.

debrief: High beams whenever there are no oncoming vehicles; regular headlights when there are or when you are following. Dim 500 feet before oncoming and 300 feet behind. Drive at a speed that lets you stop inside the glow — usually 400 feet. Take the twenty-minute nap.

source.teaching_target: 2.5: '500 feet in front of an oncoming vehicle. 300 feet when you're behind.' 5.6: 'stop within the glow of your headlights (usually 400 feet).' 3.1: the 20-minute nap.
